title: Life in one line, on the live page
summary: The same Life lesson told with the live page itself: the published demo recorded while a script steps through it.

scenes.heading: Life in one line
scenes.narration: Conway's Game of Life, in a single line of code.
lines: Conway's Game of Life, in X_eTaL.
The whole rule is one line of array code.

scenes.heading: The rule: read it right to left
scenes.narration: Here is the whole rule, on the demo page. {Read|Read} it from right to left. Rotate the board, add up the copies, and compare. Each click on step moves the board one generation.

scenes.heading: 1. Nine shifted copies
scenes.narration: Rotate the board by minus one, zero, and one, in both directions. That gives nine shifted copies, one for each neighbor, and one for the cell itself.

scenes.heading: 2. Add them up
scenes.narration: Add up the nine copies. Now every cell holds its own value, plus its eight neighbors.

scenes.heading: 3. Compare
scenes.narration: A cell is alive next time when the sum is three, or when it is alive now and the sum is four.

scenes.heading: Run it: the R-pentomino
scenes.narration: Run it. Start with just five cells, on a sixteen by sixteen board that wraps around. Press play, and watch it grow, one generation after another. Every step is that same single line.
